design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 04 « PNJ » card (the BINDING target: SegmentedControl with PNJ active; « PERSONNAGE » Select; « DIALOGUE » multiline Field; « Donne un objet » Toggle). Mounted inside node-editor's action slot via ActionRegistry. Anatomy + tokens from styles.css: Select, Field, Toggle, the shared ObjectEditor. Low-fi, light theme.

plan.goal: Model a PNJ encounter on a node: pick or create the character, write its dialogue, and optionally have it grant an object — registered as the 'pnj' action type so node-editor mounts it without knowing its internals. (A future version may add a dialogue tree — designed-for, not built now.)

design_contract._binding: Rebuild § 04 PNJ with design-system components; DS tokens win over prose. Self-registers with ActionRegistry as type 'pnj'; renders only inside node-editor's action body.
design_contract.character: « PERSONNAGE » `forms/Select` that either picks an existing PNJ from the book or creates a new one (création à la volée) with a name + player-facing description.
design_contract.dialogue: « DIALOGUE » multiline `forms/Field` with an inviting placeholder; player-facing literary register.
design_contract.gives_object: « Donne un objet » `Toggle`; when on, an object picker (create new or choose from the book inventory) using the shared brain ObjectEditor — the granted object carries a name AND a player-facing description.
design_contract.future_dialogue_tree: Leave a clearly-labelled, inert extension point (« Arbre de dialogue — bientôt ») so v2 can grow a branching dialogue without reshaping this editor; do not build it now.
design_contract.empty_state: No character chosen → an inviting « Choisir ou créer un personnage » affordance (project-wide empty-state rule).

acceptance_criteria: action-pnj self-registers with ActionRegistry as type 'pnj' (label, editor component, runtime resolver) so node-editor mounts it purely from the registry; node-editor contains no PNJ-specific code.
Selecting/creating a PNJ persists the character (name + player-facing description) on the node via BookService; created PNJs are reusable within the book.
Editing the dialogue persists it on the node (player-facing text) and survives reload; empty dialogue shows an inviting placeholder.

Toggling « Donne un objet » on lets the author pick or create an object via the shared ObjectEditor; the grant persists referencing an ObjectCatalogService object id and emits object:granted{nodeId, objectId}; toggling off removes the grant.
A granted object carries both a name and a player-facing description (never a bare string), consistent with the inventory model.
The dialogue-tree extension point renders as a labelled inert affordance (no functionality), without breaking layout.
All controls render from design-system components/tokens, light theme; ≥44px targets; the editor is keyboard-navigable.
plan.walking_skeleton: Register the 'pnj' type with ActionRegistry (label + editor). Render the PNJ Select (pick/create), the dialogue Field, and the « Donne un objet » Toggle + object picker. Persist character + dialogue + grant on the node via BookService/ObjectCatalogService; emit object:granted. No dialogue-tree, no reuse-search polish yet.

iterations.goal: Register 'pnj' with ActionRegistry and build the § 04 PNJ editor: character Select (pick/create name + player description), dialogue Field with placeholder, persistence via BookService. Design-system fidelity.
Gives-object via shared ObjectEditor: toggle + create/choose object (name + player description), persist + emit object:granted; add the inert « arbre de dialogue — bientôt » extension point (KR-072).

known_risks: KR-070 — Self-registration only: action-pnj must register via ActionRegistry and never be imported by node-editor directly (the Open/Closed contract; re-asserts KR-051).
KR-071 — Granted/created objects carry a player-facing description, not just a name, and reference ObjectCatalogService by stable id (re-asserts KR-052/KR-062).
KR-072 — The future dialogue-tree is designed-for but NOT built: ship an inert, clearly-labelled extension point; do not half-build branching dialogue now (scope discipline).
KR-011 — No raw localStorage; persist via BookService/ObjectCatalogService (global config KR-111).
KR-013 — Bind controls to the store/handlers, not useEffect-mirrored prop copies (global config KR-113).
A11y — character/object pickers and toggle are keyboard-operable with ≥44px targets.

resolved_decisions: PNJ can be created on the fly OR chosen from a list of the book's PNJs (the user asked for both).
Granting an object means create-new OR pick-from-list, and objects always have a player-facing description.
Dialogue tree is a future version — extension point only, not built now (per the user's note).
open_questions: Are PNJs a book-level reusable catalog (like objects/monsters) or per-node only? (Leaning book-level reusable for consistency with monsters/objects.)
